scenes.section: Three amounts, three different meanings

lines.raw: Discount (also called "PPO savings" or contractual adjustment).
lines.say: Discount (also called "P P O savings" or contractual adjustment).

lines.raw: Discount equals Billed − Allowed.
lines.say: Discount equals Billed − Allowed.

lines.raw: For example: Billed $150 − Allowed $102 equals $48 discount.
lines.say: For example: Billed 150 dollars − Allowed 102 dollars equals 48 dollars discount.

lines.raw: The doctor cannot charge Emily this $48.
lines.say: The doctor cannot charge Emily this 48 dollars.

lines.raw: The patient's part comes from three rules in their plan:
lines.say: The patient's part comes from three rules in their plan:

scenes.section: The patient's share

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Deductible**. What it means: An amount the patient must pay **each year** before insurance starts sharing costs. Example: $1,000 per year. The first $1,000 of allowed costs are on Emily.
lines.say: Deductible. What it means: An amount the patient must pay each year before insurance starts sharing costs. Example: 1000 dollars per year. The first 1000 dollars of allowed costs are on Emily.

lines.raw: **Copay**. What it means: A **fixed amount** paid for certain services. Example: $25 for every doctor visit.
lines.say: Copay. What it means: A fixed amount paid for certain services. Example: 25 dollars for every doctor visit.

lines.raw: **Coinsurance**. What it means: A **percentage** split after the deductible. Example: 80/20 plan: insurer pays 80%, Emily pays 20%. Just like Sita's 20% share in SSF!
lines.say: Coinsurance. What it means: A percentage split after the deductible. Example: 80/20 plan: insurer pays 80 percent, Emily pays 20 percent. Just like Sita's 20 percent share in S S F!

lines.raw: **Out-of-pocket maximum**. What it means: The **most** a patient pays in a year. After this, insurance pays 100%. Example: $5,000 per year.
lines.say: Out-of-pocket maximum. What it means: The most a patient pays in a year. After this, insurance pays 100 percent. Example: 5000 dollars per year.

scenes.section: The patient's share

lines.raw: The key relationship.
lines.say: The key relationship.

lines.raw: Allowed equals Paid plus Deductible plus Copay plus Coinsurance.
lines.say: Allowed equals Paid plus Deductible plus Copay plus Coinsurance.

lines.raw: For example: So: Paid equals Allowed − (Deductible plus Copay plus Coinsurance).
lines.say: For example: So: Paid equals Allowed − (Deductible plus Copay plus Coinsurance).

lines.raw: Premium is not on the claim.
lines.say: Premium is not on the claim.

lines.raw: The **premium** is the monthly fee to keep insurance active, like Sita's monthly SSF contribution.
lines.say: The premium is the monthly fee to keep insurance active, like Sita's monthly S S F contribution.

lines.raw: It is paid whether you get sick or not, so it never appears on a claim.
lines.say: It is paid whether you get sick or not, so it never appears on a claim.

lines.raw: With private insurance:
lines.say: With private insurance:

lines.raw: Ram's bill is Rs 2,000 (**billed**).
lines.say: Ram's bill is Rs 2,000 (billed).

lines.raw: He pays all of it at the counter first.
lines.say: He pays all of it at the counter first.

lines.raw: He claims it from his insurer.
lines.say: He claims it from his insurer.

lines.raw: His policy does not cover the Rs 200 registration/file charge, so the insurer **allows Rs 1,800**.
lines.say: His policy does not cover the Rs 200 registration/file charge, so the insurer allows Rs 1,800.

lines.raw: The insurer **reimburses Rs 1,800** to Ram (the **paid** amount).
lines.say: The insurer reimburses Rs 1,800 to Ram (the paid amount).

lines.raw: Ram's own cost is **Rs 200**, the part that was **not covered**.
lines.say: Ram's own cost is Rs 200, the part that was not covered.

lines.raw: Key difference from the US and SSF: the money goes back to **Ram**, not to the hospital.
lines.say: Key difference from the U S and S S F: the money goes back to Ram, not to the hospital.

lines.raw: With the Social Security Fund:
lines.say: With the Social Security Fund:

lines.raw: Sita's visit costs Rs 2,000.
lines.say: Sita's visit costs Rs 2,000.

lines.raw: SSF checks each item against its **approved rates**.
lines.say: S S F checks each item against its approved rates.

lines.raw: All items are within SSF rates, so the **allowed** amount is Rs 2,000.
lines.say: All items are within S S F rates, so the allowed amount is Rs 2,000.

lines.raw: (If the hospital charged more than SSF's rate, SSF would only count its own rate.).
lines.say: (If the hospital charged more than SSF's rate, S S F would only count its own rate.).

lines.raw: Sita pays **20% = Rs 400**.
lines.say: Sita pays 20 percent = Rs 400.

lines.raw: That is her **cost sharing**, the same idea as US **coinsurance**.
lines.say: That is her cost sharing, the same idea as U S coinsurance.

lines.raw: SSF pays **80% = Rs 1,600** to the hospital, as long as Sita is within her **yearly medical limit**.
lines.say: S S F pays 80 percent = Rs 1,600 to the hospital, as long as Sita is within her yearly medical limit.

lines.raw: Items SSF does not cover, or costs above the limit, are also Sita's to pay.
lines.say: Items S S F does not cover, or costs above the limit, are also Sita's to pay.

lines.raw: The yearly limit works like the reverse of a US out-of-pocket maximum: in the US the **patient's** spending has a cap; in SSF the **fund's** spending on you has a cap.
lines.say: The yearly limit works like the reverse of a U S out-of-pocket maximum: in the U S the patient's spending has a cap; in S S F the fund's spending on you has a cap.

lines.raw: Why a service is not allowed (denied), and who pays.
lines.say: Why a service is not allowed (denied), and who pays.

lines.raw: **Plan does not cover it**. Example: Cosmetic surgery, like a nose job for looks only. Who pays?: **Patient**: the plan never covered it.
lines.say: Plan does not cover it. Example: Cosmetic surgery, like a nose job for looks only. Who pays?: Patient: the plan never covered it.

lines.raw: **Patient not covered** on that date. Example: Visit after the insurance ended. Who pays?: **Patient**: there was no active plan.
lines.say: Patient not covered on that date. Example: Visit after the insurance ended. Who pays?: Patient: there was no active plan.

lines.raw: **Provider not allowed to do that service**. Example: A physiotherapist bills for surgery, or a provider bills for something outside their licence. Who pays?: **Provider**: usually cannot bill the patient.
lines.say: Provider not allowed to do that service. Example: A physiotherapist bills for surgery, or a provider bills for something outside their licence. Who pays?: Provider: usually cannot bill the patient.

lines.raw: **Provider sanctioned by the government**. Example: A doctor banned (excluded) from Medicare for fraud still sends claims. Who pays?: **Provider**: the insurer cannot pay them.
lines.say: Provider sanctioned by the government. Example: A doctor banned (excluded) from Medicare for fraud still sends claims. Who pays?: Provider: the insurer cannot pay them.

scenes.section: Package prices on hospital claims: DRG and APC

lines.raw: DRG (Diagnosis Related Group).
lines.say: D R G (Diagnosis Related Group).

lines.raw: A **3-digit group** for a whole **inpatient** stay.
lines.say: A 3-digit group for a whole inpatient stay.

lines.raw: Similar stays (for example, "appendix removal without complications") share one DRG and one fixed payment, however many days or tablets were used.
lines.say: Similar stays (for example, "appendix removal without complications") share one D R G and one fixed payment, however many days or tablets were used.

lines.raw: Software called a **grouper** picks the DRG from the diagnoses, procedures, age and discharge details.
lines.say: Software called a grouper picks the D R G from the diagnoses, procedures, age and discharge details.

lines.raw: APC (Ambulatory Payment Classification).
lines.say: A P C (Ambulatory Payment Classification).

lines.raw: Medicare's package groups for **outpatient** hospital services, such as an ER visit or a day surgery.
lines.say: Medicare's package groups for outpatient hospital services, such as an E R visit or a day surgery.

scenes.section: Key takeaways

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: **Billed** = provider's price.
lines.say: Billed = provider's price.

lines.raw: **Allowed** = insurer's accepted price.
lines.say: Allowed = insurer's accepted price.

lines.raw: **Paid** = what insurer pays.
lines.say: Paid = what insurer pays.

lines.raw: Discount = Billed − Allowed.
lines.say: Discount = Billed − Allowed.

lines.raw: In-network providers cannot charge the patient this difference.
lines.say: In-network providers cannot charge the patient this difference.

lines.raw: Patient share = Deductible + Copay + Coinsurance (+ anything not covered).
lines.say: Patient share = Deductible and Copay and Coinsurance (+ anything not covered).

lines.raw: Allowed = Paid + Patient share.
lines.say: Allowed = Paid and Patient share.

lines.raw: Hospital stays may be paid as a package: **DRG** for inpatient, **APC** for Medicare outpatient.
lines.say: Hospital stays may be paid as a package: D R G for inpatient, A P C for Medicare outpatient.

lines.raw: Total these payments by claim.
lines.say: Total these payments by claim.
